user_input: Someone logged into my Instagram account without my permission and changed the password.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 43 (unauthorized access, civil liability); IT Act Section 66 (computer-related offences, if dishonest/fraudulent intent)
procedure_where_to_go: File a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in under 'Hacking/Unauthorized Access'. Also report to the platform's grievance officer for account recovery. If financial loss is involved, also call 1930.
notes: Ask user to preserve login-alert emails/screenshots as evidence.

user_input: My laptop got hacked and someone installed a virus that deleted my files.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 43 (damage to computer system, data); IT Act Section 66 (dishonest/fraudulent computer-related offence)
procedure_where_to_go: Report at cybercrime.gov.in; consider filing an FIR at the local cyber cell if financial/business loss occurred.

user_input: Someone accessed my company email account and is reading my confidential mails.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 43; IT Act Section 66; IT Act Section 70 if it is a protected/critical system
procedure_where_to_go: Report to cybercrime.gov.in and inform your organization's IT/security team immediately; escalate to local cyber cell if data was leaked externally.
notes: Employer-related incidents may also trigger internal disciplinary/data-breach procedures.

user_input: My WhatsApp got hacked through a fake QR code and now they are messaging my contacts.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 43; IT Act Section 66; IT Act Section 66D if impersonation/fraud is used against contacts
procedure_where_to_go: Immediately log out of all WhatsApp Web sessions, reset account via WhatsApp support, then file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
notes: Time-sensitive — advise immediate account security steps alongside legal reporting.

user_input: Someone is controlling my phone remotely, I think there's spyware installed on it.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 43; IT Act Section 66; IT Act Section 66E if privacy/personal data is being accessed
procedure_where_to_go: Report at cybercrime.gov.in; consider a factory reset after backing up evidence; approach local cyber cell if it involves a known person (e.g., ex-partner) for potential stalking charges too.
notes: Cross-check against Cyberstalking category if perpetrator is known and pattern of surveillance exists.

user_input: I got a call saying my bank account will be blocked, I shared my OTP and now money is missing from my account.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66C (identity theft); IT Act Section 66D (cheating by personation using computer resource)
procedure_where_to_go: Call the 1930 cyber fraud helpline IMMEDIATELY to attempt a transaction freeze, then file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in. Also inform your bank's fraud department right away.
notes: Time-critical — the 1930 helpline is only effective within a short window after the fraudulent transaction.

user_input: Someone sent me a fake link pretending to be from my bank and I entered my card details.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66C; IT Act Section 66D
procedure_where_to_go: Call 1930 immediately, block your card via bank helpline, then file a report at cybercrime.gov.in with the phishing link/screenshot as evidence.

user_input: I paid for something on a fake online shopping website and never received the product or a refund.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66D (cheating by personation); BNS cheating provisions may also apply
procedure_where_to_go: File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in under financial fraud; also file a consumer complaint on the National Consumer Helpline / e-daakhil if it's a genuine but non-delivering seller vs outright fraud.
notes: Distinguish fraud (police/cybercrime route) from a genuine consumer dispute (consumer forum route) based on intent.

user_input: My UPI app shows a payment I never made, someone must have cloned my SIM.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66C (identity theft); IT Act Section 66D
procedure_where_to_go: Call 1930 immediately, contact your telecom provider to check for SIM swap, then file at cybercrime.gov.in and inform your bank.
notes: SIM-swap cases are time-critical — telecom provider report should happen in parallel with cyber complaint.

user_input: Someone posing as a company HR offered me a work-from-home job and asked me to pay a 'registration fee', now they are unreachable.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66D (cheating by personation)
procedure_where_to_go: File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in; call 1930 if payment was made recently and freezing is still possible.

user_input: Someone edited my photo into a nude picture and is threatening to post it online.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66E (violation of privacy); IT Act Section 67/67A (obscene/sexually explicit material)
procedure_where_to_go: File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in (has a dedicated women/children safety reporting section); also file an FIR at the local cyber cell given the threat element.
notes: This may overlap with Sextortion category if there is a demand attached — check for blackmail language.

user_input: My ex shared my private photos in a group chat without my consent.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66E (privacy violation); IT Act Section 67/67A if the images are sexually explicit
procedure_where_to_go: Report at cybercrime.gov.in immediately; request the platform's grievance officer to take down the content under IT Rules 2021; consider filing an FIR.

user_input: Someone took a screenshot of my private video call and is now circulating it.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66E; IT Act Section 67/67A
procedure_where_to_go: File at cybercrime.gov.in; request urgent takedown via platform grievance officer; approach local cyber cell for an FIR.

user_input: A stranger got my private photos during a video call and is now demanding money or they'll leak them.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66E (privacy violation); IT Act Section 67A (sexually explicit material); BNS extortion and criminal intimidation sections
procedure_where_to_go: Do NOT pay. Report immediately at cybercrime.gov.in and call 1930 if any payment was already made. File an FIR at the local cyber cell given the extortion threat.
notes: High-urgency case — advise the user not to engage further with the blackmailer and to preserve all chat evidence.

user_input: My former partner is threatening to post our private pictures unless I get back with them.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66E; IT Act Section 67A; BNS criminal intimidation sections
procedure_where_to_go: File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in and approach the local cyber cell/police station for an FIR given the ongoing threat.

user_input: Someone is blackmailing me with a fake nude image made using AI, demanding I send more photos.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66E; IT Act Section 66D (impersonation via fake/deepfake content); BNS extortion sections
procedure_where_to_go: Report at cybercrime.gov.in; do not comply with demands; file an FIR at local cyber cell; preserve all communication as evidence.
notes: Deepfake-specific cases are an emerging category — flag for the platform's takedown process too.

user_input: I found sexual content involving a child being shared in a chat group I'm part of.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 67B (mandatory reporting — non-negotiable escalation)
procedure_where_to_go: This must be reported IMMEDIATELY at cybercrime.gov.in (dedicated CSAM reporting category) and to CHILDLINE 1098. Do not download, save, or forward the content.
notes: Hard-routed category — system should never present this as optional advice; always escalate regardless of conversational flow.

user_input: My child received inappropriate sexual messages and images from an adult online.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 67B; POCSO Act provisions
procedure_where_to_go: Report immediately at cybercrime.gov.in and call CHILDLINE 1098. Consider filing an FIR at the local police station without delay.
notes: Overlaps with Cyberbullying of a Minor category — treat as CSAM/POCSO priority given the sexual solicitation element.

user_input: An unknown person keeps messaging and calling me repeatedly even after I asked them to stop.
applicable_statute_sections: BNS stalking provisions (replacing former IPC 354D); BNS criminal intimidation sections if threats are involved. Note: IT Act Section 66A is struck down (unconstitutional per Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, 2015) and must not be cited.
procedure_where_to_go: File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in; approach the local police station to file an FIR under the relevant BNS stalking/harassment sections.
notes: Explicit negative constraint: never cite Section 66A as applicable law.

user_input: Someone I don't know is sending me threatening messages on social media.
applicable_statute_sections: BNS criminal intimidation sections; IT Act Section 66E if private information/images are also involved. Section 66A is void — do not cite.
procedure_where_to_go: Report at cybercrime.gov.in; file an FIR at the local cyber cell/police station given the threat.

user_input: My coworker keeps tracking my social media activity and shows up wherever I post I'll be.
applicable_statute_sections: BNS stalking provisions; BNS criminal intimidation sections if accompanied by threats
procedure_where_to_go: File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in; consider an FIR at the local police station, and inform HR/workplace if the coworker is from the same organization.

user_input: Someone created a fake Instagram account using my name and photos and is messaging my friends.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66D (cheating by personation); BNS cheating and forgery sections
procedure_where_to_go: Report the fake profile to the platform directly for takedown, and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.

user_input: A fake LinkedIn profile using my company designation is contacting my clients for money.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66D; BNS cheating and forgery sections
procedure_where_to_go: File at cybercrime.gov.in; report to the platform's grievance officer for urgent takedown; notify affected clients/your organization.

user_input: Someone created a matrimonial profile using my pictures without my knowledge.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66D; IT Act Section 66E (privacy violation); BNS cheating/forgery sections
procedure_where_to_go: Report to the platform for takedown; file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in; consider an FIR at local cyber cell.

user_input: I got an email saying my personal data was leaked in a breach from an e-commerce site I used.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 43A (compensation for negligence in protecting sensitive data); DPDPA 2023 (if it qualifies as a data-fiduciary breach)
procedure_where_to_go: File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in; once DPDPA grievance mechanisms/Data Protection Board are operational, a complaint can also be filed there against the data fiduciary.
notes: Note current implementation status of DPDPA rules/Data Protection Board when advising on this route, since it was still rolling out.

user_input: My Aadhaar and PAN details are being misused to open accounts I never applied for.
applicable_statute_sections: IT Act Section 66C (identity theft); IT Act Section 43A if traced to a company's negligence; BNS cheating/forgery sections
procedure_where_to_go: File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in; report to the relevant bank/UIDAI grievance portal; file a police FIR given identity theft.

user_input: Someone posted false statements about me and my business on social media, damaging my reputation.
applicable_statute_sections: BNS defamation sections (both civil and criminal routes may apply)
procedure_where_to_go: You can pursue a civil defamation suit for damages, or file a criminal complaint at the local police station/cybercrime.gov.in. Platform takedown can also be requested via the grievance officer under IT Rules 2021.
notes: Flag the civil vs criminal distinction to the user — criminal defamation requires proving intent/knowledge of falsity, civil suit focuses on damages.

user_input: A former employee is posting fake negative reviews about my shop online to hurt my business.
applicable_statute_sections: BNS defamation sections; IT Rules 2021 platform takedown mechanism
procedure_where_to_go: Report to the review platform for takedown; consult on filing a civil defamation suit; can also file at cybercrime.gov.in if it involves impersonation or fake accounts.

user_input: My teenage sibling is being constantly mocked and threatened by classmates in an online group.
applicable_statute_sections: POCSO Act overlap (if any sexual element); BNS criminal intimidation/harassment sections; IT Act Section 67B only if sexual content is involved
procedure_where_to_go: Report at cybercrime.gov.in (child safety category); call CHILDLINE 1098; inform the school administration.
notes: Escalation path should prioritize CHILDLINE and school involvement alongside legal reporting.

user_input: A group of students created a fake account to humiliate my child at school.
applicable_statute_sections: BNS cheating/forgery (fake profile) sections; BNS criminal intimidation/harassment sections
procedure_where_to_go: Report the fake account to the platform for takedown; file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in; inform the school and consider CHILDLINE 1098 if distress is significant.
